key_insight: This paper presents COSA-GS, a practical compression approach for 3D Gaussian Splatting that avoids brittle spatial-context modeling while keeping decoding reliable across platforms. The key idea is to make 3DGS much smaller without sacrificing the robustness needed for real-world deployment.
problem_solved: 3D Gaussian Splatting produces high-quality novel-view synthesis, but its models are storage-heavy and existing compression methods are often too complex and fragile. In particular, prior approaches depend on irregular 3D spatial context and floating-point inference, which can increase training/coding complexity and cause cross-platform entropy-decoding failures.
method: Builds context without relying on spatial aggregation over irregular 3D structures, reducing modeling complexity.
Uses a more practical coding/compression design that is easier to train and deploy.
Avoids floating-point context inference issues to improve numerical consistency and decoding reliability across different hardware/software platforms.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes 3DGS more deployable in real systems by lowering storage cost and reducing the risk of decoding errors. It is especially relevant for mobile, edge, and cross-platform rendering workflows where robustness and efficiency matter.
